summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would extend interim appointment and entitlement arrangements for the Chief Judge Advocate and one full time judge advocate in the Australian Defence Force.
It would add two years to the existing arrangements, allowing tenure of up to six years unless the Defence Minister specifies an earlier termination day.
Most provisions would start on Royal Assent, while appointment-limit clarifications would operate retrospectively from 22 September 2009 to address uncertainty about the existing appointments.
changes: The statutory five-year appointment limit would be disapplied to the Chief Judge Advocate appointed under the interim legislation.
The three-year panel appointment limit would be disapplied to the judge advocate covered by the interim arrangements.
Associated payment rules would be updated to refer to the extended six-year period.
The Minister's window for declaring a termination day would extend from four years to six.
summary.affected: The Chief Judge Advocate, the covered full time judge advocate and the Minister for Defence are affected.

speeches.speaker: Stuart Robert
speeches.brief: Criticised the government for still not having a permanent Military Justice bill four years after the High Court's 2009 Lane v Morrison decision struck down the Australian Military Court, noting Minister Faulkner had called fixing military justice the government's highest priority yet only interim measures bills have followed.

speeches.speaker: Graham Perrett
speeches.brief: Supported the bill as a RAAF reserve legal officer himself, explained the Australian Military Court was established in 2006 with a chief military judge, two permanent judges and a reserve panel before being struck down in the Lane and Morrison case, and praised ADF personnel operating in extreme conditions such as 51 degree heat in Afghanistan.

speeches.speaker: Jane Prentice
speeches.brief: Explained the interim measures extend judicial tenure by two years pending a permanent Military Court, noted the Howard government implemented 32 of 40 recommendations when establishing the Australian Military Court in 2007, and said Labor's more than $25 billion in defence cuts have left the defence industry workforce at just 24,000 to 25,000 jobs, far below the 34,000 predicted for 2013.

speeches.speaker: Mike Kelly
speeches.brief: Summed up the bill, confirming it extends the tenure of the Chief Judge Advocate and judge advocate's panel by a further two years beyond their September expiry, and rejected opposition criticism by pointing to increased defence spending in this year's budget.

speeches.speaker: Gary Humphries
speeches.brief: The Military Justice (Interim Measures) Amendment Bill 2013 extends the tenure of the Chief Judge Advocate and other statutory office holders by two years, supported by the coalition to maintain the status quo while a permanent military court is developed. The speaker urged parliament not to delay, stressing the need for surety and clear processes for ADF personnel, especially those in combat zones.
